title: Google began as an eigenvector problem
body: PageRank scored a page by the scores of pages linking to it, a circular definition resolved by eigenvector maths on the link graph. Random-surfer probabilities settle into a ranking that was far harder to spam than counting keywords. Brin and Page's 1998 paper turned a linear-algebra exercise into a company.
source_hint: Brin and Page, 'The Anatomy of a Large-Scale Hypertextual Web Search Engine' (1998)
